First Appeal No. 25 of 2015.
Civil Rule No. 45(FA) 2015.
lawyer:
Nahid Yesmin with lqbal Hossain, Advocates-------For the Plaintiff-Appellants. 
Delowar Hossain, Senior Advocate with Lily Rani Saha, Advocates------For the Defendant-Respondents.
parties:
Khokon Chandra Bhawal and others-------Plaintiff-Appellants
Vs
Md Gias Uddin and others--------Defendant-Respondents
full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 dismissing the suit.

2. The appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 against the respondents as defendants for declaration of title in respect of suit land and further declaration that the compromise decree passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is illegal, collusive, void, and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. During pendency of appeal the appellant No. 9 died on 14-8-2016 and his legal heirs has been duly substituted by order of this court dated 14-12-2016.

4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land of CS plot No. 1827 measuring 50 decimals along with other lands was originally belonged to Nizamuddin and accordingly CS Khatian No. 142 was recorded in his name. Nizamuddin transferred the suit land by registered Mortgage Deed being No. 5146 on 29-8-1925 to one Wahed Ali. An amicable partition was made among the brothers of Wahed Ali in respect of suit land along with other undisputed lands and through an amicable partition Durjon, brother of Wahed Ali got the suit land. Durjan died leaving behind two sons namely, Jinnat Ali and Habibullah who later on sold the suit land to one Alim Mia son of Jonab Ali by registered Kabala No. 1836 dated 18-1-1956 and delivered possession to him, accordingly RS khatian No. 322 was prepared in the name of Mid alias Alimuddin. Alim Mia transferred the entire suit land by registered hebanama being No. 2582 on 14-6-1987 in favour of his wife Rabeya Khatoon, three sons—Sirajul, Samsul Hoq, Md Ramjan Hossain and four daughters—Hasenur Begum, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon and Shaheena Begum. In this way Rabeya and Ramjan got 15 decimals and 10 decimals of the suit land respectively. In the same way Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon got together 11.15 decimals and Shaheena Begum got 13.75 decimals of land in the suit land. Subsequently Rabeya, Ramjan, Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon mutated their names by declaration Deed No. 1148 dated 25-5-1993 and paid rents to the Government. Halima Khatoon sold her portion i.e 3 decimals of the suit land to one Abdul Ali by registered kabala being No. 3908 on 7-9-1995. Mst Shaheena Begum extinguished her share from the suit land by selling her portion to plaintiff No. 1, 2 and 3 through three registered Kabala Nos. 2669, 2670, 2671 all dated 18-7-1999 in equal share. Abdul Ali, who purchased the suit land from Halima sold his entire portion to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by registered kabala No. 1031 on 1-4-2001. In this way the plaintiff No. 1-2 got 6 decimal each and plaintiff No. 3 got 51/4 decimals of land. Fatema Khatoon daughter of Alimuddin sold her entire share of suit land to Mafizul Islam, plaintiff No. 4 by saf-kabala on 12-9-1999. Ramjan (defendant No. 15) who got from his father Alimuddin by way of heba sold 3 decimals to plaintiff No.5 on 26-5-1999. Most. Rabeya, who got 15 decimals of land from her husband sold to the plaintiff Nos. 6-9 through three Kabalas on 23-6-1999. Hasenur Begum, who also got by heba sold it to one Habibullah and thereafter Habibullah sold it to the plaintiff No. 10 through Kabala No. 6568 on 9-12-2007. Ramjan (defendant No.15) and Halima Khatoon sold their remaining portion of land to the plaintiff No.11. Thus the plaintiffs have been possessing the entire suit land by mutating, paying rents, planting crops and taking loan from bank by mortgaging the suit land. The defendants were trying to demolish the boundary, then the plaintiffs filed the petition case No. 639 dated 1-12-2010. Thereafter the defendants were trying to disposes the plaintiffs and on 1-8-2010 the defendants disclosed that they got title over the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009, wherein the defendant Nos. 1-12 of the present suit as plaintiffs filed said Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 impleading the present defendant Nos. 4-7 and 13-15 as defendants.

5. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-11 con-tested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They denied material averments made in the plaint. The case of the defendants are that the suit land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin who died leaving behind two sons namely, Jonab Ali and Kamfu Mia. Janab Ali died leaving behind four sons namely, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Ameer Ali and Jamir All and two daughters namely, Topi Bibi, Aleshi Bibi. SA Khatian 321 was prepared in the name of Kamfu Mia and the aforesaid heirs of Jonab Ali. While in possession of 50% share i.e 25 decimals of suit land, Kamfu Mia died leaving behind wife Aimon Bibi and only son Hossain Mia. After death of Aimon bibi, Hossain ali got the share of Kamfu Mia and possessed the southern 25 decimals of the suit land. Hossain Ali died leaving behind six sons defendant Nos. 1-6 and one daughter defendant No. 11. Elachi bibi, daughter of Jonab Ali died leaving behind 4 brothers-Ameer Ali, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Jamir Ali and one sister Tohi Bibi. Ameer Ali died leaving behind 2 sons namely, Anwar Hossain, Amjad Hossain and one daughter Sahnaj i.e defendant Nos: 8-10. Thus defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 along with defendant No. 11 have been possessing 31decimals of land together with another piece of land by planting crops. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 executed power of attorney infavour of defendant No. 11 and 12 on 8-10-09 to look after the land and to deal with the suits. The defendants 1-6, 8-10 and 11 went to Tohsil Office to mutate their names and knew about wrong recording of RS Khatian in plaintiffs names. Thereafter the aforesaid defendants filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 2010 in which their names has been mutated and accordingly they paid tax, rent etc. The further case of the defendants is that Nizamuddin took loan 200 from one Wahed Ali subject to payment of 2% interest per month and accordingly a registered deed was executed between them on 29-8-1925. Subsequently, Nizamuddin paid the entire loan money to Wahid Ali and SA record was correctly prepared in the name of the heirs of Nizamuddin. Thus all the successive transfers were made on the basis of the said deed dated 29-8-1925 are illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the defendants.

6. The Trial Court had framed the issues in the following manner:—

১।অত্র মোকদ্দমা বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে সচল কিনা?

বাদীপক্ষের প্রাইমাফেসি টাইটেল আছে কিনা?

৩।বাদীপক্ষের অপূরণীয় ক্ষতির সম্ভাবনা আছে কিনা?

৪।সুবিধা অসুবিধা ভারসাম্য বাদীপক্ষের অনুকূলে আছে কিনা।

৫।বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থনা মোতাবেক ডিক্রী পাইতে পারে কিনা?

7. In the suit, the plaintiffs examined 6(six) PWs including the plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1. The defendants in support of their case examined 2 DWs including defendant No. 11 as DW 1. Documents filed by the plaintiffs were marked as Exhibits 1-9 and the documents filed by the defendants were marked as Exhibits-ka-um (series). The learned Joint District Judge, after considering the oral and documentary evidence dismissed the suit.

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiffs preferred this appeal.

9. Ms Nahid Yesmin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-appellants primarily submits that the court below erroneously held that Deed No. 5146 dated 28-8-1925 (Exhibit-8(4) executed by Nizamuddin is not a mortgage deed but “জোত জমি বিক্রয় সুদি রেহানী” which effects or purports to effect the sale and said transaction cannot be treated as Mortgage as per section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. She further submits that the learned Joint District Judge below failed to consider the oral and documentary evidence by which the plaintiffs were successfully proved their title and possession over the suit land. She finally argued further that the learned court below has committed gross illegality in not considering the stipulation made in the Deed in question that Nizamuddin sold the suit land, not mortgage the same to Wahid Ali.

10. Today 31-10-2018 this appeal was fixed for delivery of judgment. Learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-Appellants with permission of the court further argued on some issues. She departed from her earlier argument that the deed in question dated 25-8-1925 is not a Deed of sale, but Mortgage by conditional sale. She argued that though there was no condition of sale embodied in the said deed but intention to sale exists there which deals with mortgage by conditional sale. She also argued that one Alim Mia, legal heirs of Nizamuddin sold the suit land to the legal heirs of Wahed Ali which clearly proved that by the said Deed the heirs of Wahid Ali became owner of the suit land. In support of her submissions, she referred decisions reported in AIR Nagpur 264 and 44 DLR (AD) 83.

11. Mr Md Delowar Hossain, the learned senior Advocate appearing for defendants respondents submits that the deed in question is a mortgage deed which purports to create a simple mortgage as the conditions mentioned in section 58(b) of the Transfer of Property Act. He submits further that no stipulation has been contained in the aforesaid deed that the mortgagor Nizamuddin delivered possession of the suit property to mortgagee, Wahid Ali. It was further stipulated that mortgagor took loan Taka 200 from the mortgagee subject to payment of 2% interest per month and the same loan will be returned to the mortgagee within Chaitra 1332 BS. It was also stipulated that in case of failure to pay the loan money, the mortgagee shall have right to get the property with intervention of the court. He next submits that the plaintiffs have miserably failed to produce any oral and documentary evidence to prove their title and possession of the suit land. He also submits that since the plaintiffs failed to prove by oral or documentary that the mortgagor Nizamuddin failed to pay loan with interest and the mortgagee got the suit land in auction through court, rather it was evident that SA Khatian was prepared in the name of legal heirs of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the title and possession of Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants in the suit land. He further submits that the schedule of the present suit and the schedule of the earlier Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 are same and all the defendants were made parties either as plaintiffs or defendants in both the suits. The suit land on which the plaintiff claimed their title but their predecessors Wahed Ali did not acquire any title and possession. He finally submits that the court below has not committed error of law and facts and rightly found that the deed in question neither a Sale Deed nor a Deed of Mortgage by conditional sale.

12. We have heard the submissions and counter submissions of the learned Advocate of the contesting parties. Perused the oral and documentary evidence, relevant provisions of law and also citations referred by the parties.

13. From plain reading of the pleadings, documents produced and oral evidence adduced before court, it is admitted that the suit land measuring 50 decimals of land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants, who executed a registered mortgage deed dated 29-8-1925 in favour of one Wahed Ali, Predecessors of the plaintiffs in respect of suit land by taking Taka 200 as loan subject to payment of interest @ 2% pin till realization of money. There was a clear stipulation for payment of interest on repayment of loan amount and in case of failure to repayment within specified time, 30th Chaitra, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgaged property to be sold with intervention of the court.

14. It is contented by the plaintiffs that Nizamuddin could not pay the money taken as loan from Wahed Ali and thus Wahed Ali became the owner of the suit land. Thereafter, an amicable partition was made among the brothers of Wahed Ali in respect of suit land along with other lands. Durjon, the brother of Wahed Ali got the suit land by dint of amicable partition, subsequently the legal heirs of Durjon transferred the entire suit land to different persons on different dates. Ultimately, the plaintiffs got the entire suit land by successive transfers.

15. On the other hand, the defendants contended that Nizamuddin paid entire loan money taken from Wahed Ali. After the death of Nizamuddin, his two sons Kamfu Mia and Jonab Ali inherited the suit land and thereafter the defendants as their legal heirs got the suit land.

16. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 5146 dated 29-8-1925 (Exhibit-8/4) the basic document upon which the plaintiffs based their title is a Simple Mortgage or Mortgage by conditional sale.

17. To determine this question, we like to quote the relevant portion of the Mortgage Deed which reads as under:

“এইক্ষণ আমার টাকার প্রয়োজন বশত আপনার নিকট হইতে নগদ মং ২০০ টাকা কর্জ্জ গ্রহণ করিয়া অঙ্গীকার করিতেছি যে উক্ত টাকার সুদ শতকরা মাসিক ২ টাকা হিসাবে দিব ৫ ফর্দে বর্তমান সনের মাহে চৈত্র ময় সুদ আসল টাকা পরিশোধ করিব অন্যথায় টাকা আদায়ের শেষ তারিখ পর্যন্ত | উপরোক্ত হারে সুদ দিব। উক্ত সুদসহ সম্যক টাকা  আদায়ের সাফ করিতে আমার স্বত্ব দখলীর নিন | তফসীলের লিখিত অসহাই জমার রায়তি জোত স্বত্বের নাল জমি অত্র রেহানে আবদ্ধ রাখিলাম। উক্ত টাকা  আদায় না হওয়া পর্যন্ত এ সম্পত্তি অন্যত্র রেহান দান বিক্রয় মালিকানা ইস্তফা ইত্যাদি রেহানী স্বত্বের হানি জনক কোন কার্যা করি নাই । অথবা করিতে পারিব না।

করিলে আদালত অগ্রাহ্য হইবে । আর আপনার টাকা  আদায় না করিলে যথা সময়ে আদালতে নালিশ নিলাম লইতে পারিবেন।”

It appears from the recital of the document that:

i) the existence of debt,

ii) the period of repayment open ended i.e. long period,

iii) possession was not handed over,

iv) a stipulation for interest on repayment,

v) default of payment will be realized by selling the mortgaged property through auction by court of law.

<u>18. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates, Now we can look into the definition of Mortgage which is dealt in section 58 of The Transfer Property Act.</u>

<u>Section 58. "Mortgage", "mortgagor", "mortgagee", "mortgagemoney" and "mortgagedeed" defined. (a) A mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability.</u>

<u>19. The transferor is called a mortgagor, the transferee a mortgagee; the principal money and interest of which payment is secured for the time being are called the mortgage-money, and the instrument (if any) by which the transfer is effected is called a mortgage-deed.</u>

<u>20. There are 6 kinds of mortgage. Those are, Simple Mortgage, Mortgage by conditional sale, Usufructuary mortgage, English mortgage, Mortgage by deposit of title deeds and Anomalous mortgage.</u>

<u>21. As regards the nature of the deed in question raised by the parties, we like to refer only those mortgage which are necessary for proper adjudication of the present case.</u>

<u>Simple mortgage-58—(b) Where, without delivering possession of the mortgaged property, the mortgagor binds himself personally to pay the mortgage-money, and agrees, expressly or impliedly, that, in the event of his failing to pay according to his contract, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgaged property to be sold and the proceeds of sale to be applied, so far as may be necessary, in payment of the mortgage-money, the transaction is called a simple mortgage and the mortgagee a simple mortgagee."</u>

22. From the definition of Simple mortgage the following elements are found:

1. Without delivery of possession.

2. The existence of debt.

3. The period of repayment.

4. of mortgaged money, mortgaged property to be sold.

5. No actual transfer of interest or confer express power of sale.

Mortgage by conditional sale—(c) Where the mortgagor ostensibly sells the mortgaged property—

On condition that on default of payment of the mortgage-money on a certain date the sale shall become absolute, or

On condition that on such payment being made the sale shall become void, or On condition that on such payment being made the buyer shall transfer the property to the seller.

The transaction is called a mortgage by conditional sale and the mortgagee a mortgagee by conditional sale:

Provided that no such transaction shall be deemed to be a mortgage, unless the condition is embodied in the document which effects or purports to effect the sale;

The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-appellants by referring section 58(c) of Transfer of Property Act, vehemently argued that the Mortgage Deed in question (Exhibit-8/4) is in fact Mortgage by conditional sale.

23. We have perused the Mortgage Deed (Exhibit-8/4). It is clear from its recital of the deed that in case of default by the Mortgagor to pay mortgaged money, the mortgagee will have to go to court of law with a prayer for sale. That means in the eventuality the mortgaged property to be sold in auction, for payment of the mortgaged money.

24. Further recital of the deed regarding nonpayment is so clear that it cannot be interpreted in any way. Moreover, Mortgaged property was not delivered to the Mortgagor. We have carefully examined the substance of the Mortgaged Deed and find that it was a Simple mortgage and not a Mortgage by conditional sale as agitated by the learned counsel for the plaintiffs-appellants. Thus the present mortgage is not hit by the provision of section 58(c) of the Transfer of Property Act which deals with the definition of a mortgage by conditional Sale; there must be a condition that in default of payment of the mortgage money on a certain date the sale shall become absolute. But such condition is not in the embodied in the Mortgage Deed (Exhibit-8(4). It is an inviolable rule that in considering the question whether a transaction is a sale or a mortgage the court should look at the substance of deed not the form. The trial court rightly found that the Deed (Exhibit-8(4) is a simple Mortgage Deed.

25. The plaintiffs could not produce any documents which testify that the matter was interfered by any court of law or there have been auction sale by which the predecessor of the plaintiffs became the owner of the suit land.

26. The plaintiffs claimed that by successive transfers they became owner of the suit land. Since we have already observed that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Wahed Ali did not become owner of the suit land in the first place, the subsequent transfers based on the transfers by dint of deed dated 19-8-1925 needs no discussion. It is hereby mentioned that the learned Advocate argued that Alim Mia grandson of Nizamuddin purchased the entire portion of suit land from Jinnat Ali, Habibulla, son of Durjon Ali, brother of Wahed Ali. Learned Advocate for the appellants tried to submit that since Wahed Ali became the owner of the suit land and his brother Durjon who also got it by amicable partition and then his heirs sold it to Alim Mia, son of Jonab Ali. But upon examining the photocopy of the deed No. 836 dated 18-1-1956 (Exhibit-9), it looks like a mortgage deed, not a sale deed. Md Osman Gani copyist, Sadar record room, District Registered office, Narayangonj as PW 5 deposed before court. He carried the volume wherein the description of the said deed was mentioned. He compared the description of the certified copy of the said deed with the volume and found similar. But the deed filed is not certified copy, it is a photocopy of the original. In his cross-examinations he has stated that he has no knowledge about the transaction and also did not know who are transferor and transferee. The said deed was not proved in accordance of law. So, we did not find merit in the argument made by the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs.

27. In the present suit the plaintiffs filed SA khatian (Exhibit-1/1) to prove their possession in the suit land. It appears that the said khatian was prepared in the name of Kamfu, and the heirs of Jonab Ali, who are sons of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the possession of the predecessor of the defendants and not the plaintiffs. It further proved that the original owner Nizamuddin never lost his title by executing the mortgage deed in favour of Wahed Ali.

28. Apart from the Exhibit-1/1, the plaintiffs to prove their possession examined one Md Abbas Ali, uncle of the plaintiff No. 2 as PW 2, who in his cross examination could not say the boundary of the suit land. Mr Sirazul Islam PW 3 and Md Delwar Hossain PW 4 in their cross-examination could not say the number of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs quantam of land purchased by them. So, from the scrutiny the oral evidences it proved that no witnesses could say the quantum of the lands purchased by each plaintiffs and also the boundary of lands which do not prove the possession of the plaintiffs over the suit land. We have perused the Mutation Khatian, DCR, dhakilas land development tax (Exhibit-4 series) has been filed by the plaintiffs. Dhakhila, DCR, land development tax has been filed on the basis of Mutation Khatian Nos. 4632 (Exhibit-415), 16139 (Exhibit-4/7), 4690 (Exhibit-4/11). Those mutation Khatian were prepared on the basis of RS Khatian No. 322 (Exhibit-1/2). But the defendants have filed a Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 challenging that RS Khatian No. 322 was wrong. The said suit was decreed by the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 (Exhibit-5). On the basis of the said decree a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 10 Exhibit-uma(1) was initiated. In that Miscellaneous Case, Revenue Officer cancelled the Mutation Khatian prepared in the name of the plaintiffs and directed to mutate the names of the defendants in place of the plaintiffs. Against this order no step has been taken, by the plaintiff. Thus the defendants were successfully proved their possession in the suit land by filing Exhibit-uma(1).

29. The plaintiffs-appellants also prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 passed by learned Joint District Judge First Court in Title Suit No. 33J of 2009 is illegal collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Perused the said judgment (Exhibit-5). It appears that the suit lands of previous suit and the suit land of the present suit are similar. All the defendants were made parties to previous suit either as plaintiffs or defendants. But the present plaintiffs were not made parties of in the previous suit.

30. We have already held that Wahed All did not acquire any title on the basis of the alleged mortgage deed and, as such, his legal heirs has no transferable interest to execute the deeds in favour of different people on different dates in respect of the suit land. We have also found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove the deeds in accordance of law and their possession in the suit land on the basis thereof. Thus the learned Sub-ordinate Judge did not commit any error or illegality in dismissing the suit. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, of course, did not consider the prayer made by the plaintiffs as regards declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Since we have found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land as such the plaintiffs have no locus-standi to challenge the decree obtained by the defendants in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009.

31. The learned Advocate for the Appellants has cited two decisions reported in 44 DLR (AD) 84 and AIR (Nagpur) 264. We have carefully gone through the decisions but facts and circumstances of those cited decisions have no manner and application in the facts and circumstance of the present case and it will not help any way to the appellants.

32. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 is affirmed. The connected rule being Civil Rule No. 45(F) 2015 is discharged and the order of status-quo granted at the time of admission of the appeal is hereby vacated.

Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment at once.

End.
